_comment: Per-instance config for .claude/scripts/wiki-lint.py. OPTIONAL: delete this file and the linter runs on its built-in defaults, byte-for-byte identically. It exists so wiki-lint.py itself can stay byte-identical across every wiki instance, which is what lets an instance take upstream fixes with a plain checkout instead of a hand-merge. Resolved relative to --vault-root, not to the script's location. Malformed JSON, a wrong value type, or an unknown top-level key = exit 2 with a message; it never silently falls back to defaults. Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored.
_comment_merge_semantics: Each knob is MERGE (config adds to the built-ins), REPLACE (config supersedes them), or — for stale_thresholds alone — REPLACE per key, where naming one sub-key leaves the others on their built-ins. The choice is per knob and is justified in apply_config() in wiki-lint.py. Do not assume one rule for all of them.
_comment_extra_page_types: MERGE, union-only. Registers additional frontmatter `type:` values so they stop tripping FM003 'unknown type'. Each value is that type's list of REQUIRED frontmatter keys; [] means 'no required keys' and suits special pages. Union-only means two things: the six synthesis schemas (source/entity/topic/insight/plan/project) are always registered and cannot be removed from here, and naming an existing type here can only ADD required keys, never drop one. That is what makes FM004 impossible to weaken from config. Rename these entries to whatever your instance calls its special pages.
_comment_extra_stopwords: MERGE. Extra tokens ignored when `--report duplicates` compares pages. Add your org name, product names, and house vocabulary — words that appear on nearly every page and so carry no signal about whether two pages duplicate each other. Merged, not replaced, so the built-in English stopwords stay in force. Case-insensitive.
_comment_extra_non_term_bold: MERGE. Extra bold labels that `--report glossary-coverage` should NOT treat as candidate glossary terms. Add the recurring **Bold Label:** conventions your page templates use. Merged, not replaced, so the built-in labels stay in force. Case-insensitive.
_comment_tag_taxonomy: REPLACE. The closed tag vocabulary `--report tags` checks frontmatter tags against; anything outside it is reported as off-taxonomy. Replace rather than merge, because merging would leave every instance silently accepting the template's tags as valid and the report would stop catching drift. Mirror your own CLAUDE.md tag taxonomy here. Time tags (bare years, q<N>-YYYY) are matched by pattern and must not be listed. Values are lowercased on load.
_comment_orphan_allowlist: REPLACE. Vault-root-relative paths that `--report orphans` should never flag: intentional entry points that have no inbound wikilinks by design. Replace rather than merge, because these are filenames and every instance names its glossary splits and root pages differently; a whitelist you cannot shrink is not a whitelist. Log archives under wiki/log/*-archive.md are allowed automatically and need no entry.
_comment_attachment_extensions: REPLACE. Deliberately NOT set here, and you almost certainly should not set it either — this comment documents the knob, and leaving the key absent is what keeps you on the built-in list as upstream extends it. What it does: extensions of files kept in the gitignored attachments folder. An unresolvable wikilink to one is skipped by WIKI002 instead of reported broken, because the file is absent from every clone; without the skip such a link passes on your disk and fails in CI, which is a report of which machine ran the linter rather than a lint result. Set it to [] if and only if you COMMIT your attachments — they then exist in CI and the check becomes real. The built-in default is the permissive value, so this knob can only tighten WIKI002, never loosen it. Leading dots optional; lowercased on load.
_comment_stale_thresholds: REPLACE, per key — the third shape, and the only knob with it. Deliberately NOT set here, for the same reason as attachment_extensions: an absent key keeps you on the built-ins as upstream tunes them, and a copy of the defaults written out here is just a second place for them to drift. What it does: tunes `--report stale`, which is ADVISORY and never gates CI, so this is a reporting preference rather than a rule. active_days (default 90) is how long a plan/project may carry `status: active` without being touched before the page's own claim about itself looks like a lie; synthesis_days (default 365) is when an insight/topic is merely flagged as aging, which is informational since a stable page may simply be correct. A vault worked daily and one worked monthly genuinely disagree here — set it when yours does. Both keys are positive integer days; naming only one leaves the other on its built-in.
_comment_expected_h2_by_type: REPLACE. Canonical H2 section names per page type, checked by `--report schema`. Replace rather than merge, because a body schema is one whole contract copied from your CLAUDE.md; merging two instances' lists would demand the union of both and mark every page non-conforming.
